source.title: From Messy Shelves to Master Librarians: Toy-Model Exploration of Block-Diagonal Geometry in LM Activations

record.tranche_reason: The post reports toy family-tree embedding geometry, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, SAE feature completeness, or one-dimensional superposed features as defined by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The three reported toy results concern categorical clustering and linear relations in synthetic family-tree embeddings, not whether sparse features outnumbering dimensions are superposed. They are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work and proposed future SAE priors are not study results.
record.test_reason: The post measures the geometry of synthetic family-tree embeddings: block cosine similarity, sub-clusters, and linear predictability. It does not test superposition of sparse features in fewer dimensions, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE recovery in real LLMs, SAE canonicity, or feature dimensionality. Superposition and SAE results from other work are cited only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say the toy embeddings confirm categorical blocks, sub-clusters and co-linearity. They propose block-covariance, tree-Laplacian and hyperbolic priors for V-SAEs and Crosscoders on real LLM activations in later posts. Note that the title and TL;DR mention LLM activations and raw embeddings, but the only experiments reported are synthetic.
record.recipe_differences: No superposition method is applied; the reported experiments measure synthetic family-tree embedding geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sub-clustering is described after removing global distractors; no comparative sensitivity analysis is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic family-tree relation embeddings show block structure: mean intra-block cosine ≈0.72 vs off-block ≈0.18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relations from the same semantic category have more similar embeddings than relations across categories.

fits_no_version.finding: After LDA removal of distractors, the post reports sub-clusters within each block.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing global distractor directions reveals hierarchical sub-clusters within categorical embedding blocks.

fits_no_version.finding: Parent and sibling embeddings linearly predict the uncle embedding (MSE ≲1 vs ≳7 for a random target).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embeddings of compositional relational roles lie approximately in the span of their component roles.

record.problems: The post gives little detail about how the synthetic embeddings were generated or evaluated. It reports no uncertainty estimates, and the clustering evidence is qualitative; only the co-linearity result gives a comparison, to a random target.

untested.parts: No toy network with more sparse features than dimensions; no sparsity transition or superposition geometry measured.
No capacity or importance manipulation; no neuron polysemanticity measured.
No measurement of polysemantic neurons under any condition.
No real LLM activations analysed, despite the title; no SAE trained.
SAE canonicity is only cited from Meta-SAE work, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post with minimal methods detail; the source of the 'synthetic family-tree embeddings' is never specified. Its framing invokes superposition, but nothing in it tests superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test superposition in a network with more sparse features than dimensions, its sparsity-dependent transition, or the geometry of such superposed features.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Does not measure feature spreading across neurons or recover features from real LLM activations.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: synthetic family-tree embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Computed pairwise cosine similarities for parent, sibling, spouse, uncle, and grandparent, ordered by nuclear versus in-law category.
rows.measure: Mean intra-block and off-block cosine similarity
rows.locator: IV. Empirical Structure Discovery — Block-Diagonal Correlation (Prop. 1)
rows.note: The post describes two diagonal blocks and faint off-block values in these synthetic embeddings; this does not measure superposition.
rows.check: Linked correctly to no version. The text gives no information on how the embeddings were generated, and there is no baseline. The state reflects the authors' Prop. 1 (categorical blocks), not any claim version.

rows.subject: synthetic family-tree embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Projected out global distractors via LDA, then applied t-SNE and spectral clustering within each block.

conditions.value: LDA projection to remove global distractors; t-SNE; spectral clustering

rows.value: Three tight sub-clusters matching parent-child, sibling, and grandparent; similarly distinct sub-clusters in the in-law block after distractor removal
rows.locator: IV. Empirical Structure Discovery — Hierarchical Sub-Clustering (Prop. 2)
rows.note: Qualitative clustering result in the synthetic family-tree embeddings.
rows.check: Qualitative result only, after LDA distractor removal; it bears on no version.

rows.subject: synthetic family-tree embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Fit a linear regressor from z_parent and z_sibling to predict z_uncle.
rows.locator: IV. Empirical Structure Discovery — Linear Co-Linearity (Prop. 3)
rows.note: The post says the result demonstrates that uncle embeddings lie in the span of parent and sibling embeddings; it is not a test of one-dimensional superposition.
rows.check: The 'random target' baseline is loosely defined. This is linear predictability of role embeddings, not a test of 1-D superposed features (V6).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
